name_zh: 高斯-科达齐-迈纳迪方程
canonical_claim: For a smooth surface immersed in oriented Euclidean three-space, the induced first fundamental form and the second fundamental form associated to a compatible local unit normal satisfy both the Gauss curvature equation and the Codazzi-Mainardi covariant-derivative symmetry equation.
canonical_direction: necessity for forms induced by an immersion; not the converse realization theorem
domains_and_binders: A smooth two-manifold M, a smooth immersion F : M -> Euclidean R^3, a compatible local unit normal, the induced metric g, its Levi-Civita connection, and tangent vectors; exact universes, regularity, locality, and binder order remain open.
hypotheses: F is a smooth immersion into oriented Euclidean three-space
g is the metric induced by F
the chosen local normal is unit and compatible with the immersion
h is the resulting second fundamental form
conclusion: The Gauss equation and the Codazzi-Mainardi equation both hold for g and h.

alternate_encodings.target: coordinate equations for first- and second-fundamental-form coefficients
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate equivalent encoding requiring checked invariant-coordinate transports

alternate_encodings.target: Gauss-Codazzi-Ricci equations for a submanifold of arbitrary codimension
alternate_encodings.relationship: broader theorem requiring checked specialization to codimension one

alternate_encodings.target: local realization of an abstract pair (g,h) satisfying Gauss-Codazzi
alternate_encodings.relationship: converse fundamental theorem of surface theory; excluded from this root

boundary_cases: Local normal fields are permitted without global orientability. Compactness, connectedness, and embedding are not required. Non-immersions and incompatible or non-unit normal fields are excluded. Boundary regularity and tensor sign conventions remain statement-phase decisions.
